question: Validation recommends PASSED with three deferred risks and no material finding. Approve to terminal, send it back to implementation, or hold?
summary:
Recommend approve. Validation reproduced the implementation's claims rather than accepting them, on a throwaway clone and never the implementation worktree.

The end value is measured, not asserted. The adversarial revert to availability-only semantics turns the inside-and-safehouse-absent row red across all three surface tests plus both renderer tables. A real pre-change binary wrote four PATH-shim witness entries where the post-change binary created no file at all. And the durable-evidence flip was re-observed live from this sandboxed session: `status --boot --json` moves from `"sandbox":"unavailable (safehouse not on PATH)"` to `"inside (agent-safehouse)"` — the First Officer's own boot record ceasing to carry a false posture, which is the reason this task exists.

All six acceptance criteria carry reproduced evidence and every non-negotiable boundary holds under live exercise: line 1 is exactly `spacedock <version>` in all five marker cases; ambiguity reports at exit 0 while two same-host Pi markers still resolve Pi; `contract 3` keeps its value and prints below the sandbox line in-session only; both manifests retain `version: 0.26.0` with `requires-contract` gone and both binding gates green; `git diff --stat -- skills/` reports no entries. The detached adversarial audit ran on a fresh clone and came back clean.

Two judgement calls the gate should see. Both deliberate deviations from the body were accepted as moving TOWARD the approved design — notably the documentation correction, because the body's own diff contradicted AC-3's pinned marker order and would have shipped docs failing AC-6's read-back. And the surface overrun is classified DEFERRED, an estimate miss rather than material scope creep: production Go is net -8 across only approved mechanisms, with the overrun in comment and test density. Validation corrected the implementation's framing here — it is not entirely test volume; production also ran roughly 75 lines over its own estimate.

Three deferred risks are recorded with explicit promotion conditions, none blocking: `contract 3` is absent outside a detected session, so a host added without a marker row would let an integer-era skill silently false-green; the Claude and Codex launch banners read `os.Getenv` instead of the threaded env seam, identical in production today but unpinnable through `cli.Run`; and `ShortID` truncates bytes rather than runes, which matters only if a host exposes a non-ASCII session id. One polish item: the implementation report names the falsifying row incorrectly — the claim is true, the row name is not.

Approving sends this to terminal and the merge ceremony. Sending it back routes to implementation with your findings.

routes.label: Accept PASSED — advance to done and merge
Send back to implementation with findings
